title: Spark - Timestamp Timezone
question:
I have an ETL operation where I am querying a SQLServer with datetimes that are in the America/New_York timezone writing the data to a parquet and ingesting the data into a delta table via spark(spark 3.5 and delta 3.1).

As far as I can tell (reading this ref Databricks blog) the timestamp type in spark does not have any offset info written into the datetime it assumes UTC.

I am trying to figure out if we need to convert our sqlserver datetimes to UTC before writing to a table.

I have been testing changing the session timezone and it does cause confusion if I change to America/New_York and do a df.show() -- it will convert what it thinks it UTC to America/New_York and it will be the incorrect time.

However, when you df.collect() it shows the correct America/New_York time(which spark thinks is UTC?).

We are also writing data that has timestamps created with est_tz.localize(datetime.datetime(now())) the est_tz localize is created with the America/New_York timezone. The python datetime objects appear to be handled differently -- they use the driver timezone which can be different than the session assigned timezone(if you are manually setting it).

My gut is telling me to convert the datetimes to UTC(using to_utc_timestamp(ts,"America/New_York")) and when we read / present in a BI tool we need to convert to America/New_York.

Does anyone have any advice?

Thank you.
answer:
There are too many gotchas around this, which make it confusing.

Important to understand what is an "instant":

  • In programming an instant is fixed time in timeline, which can be represented in different timezones/formats. E.g. all of the following represent "a single/same instant" in time:
               1745337600 -- epoch (num seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC)
2025-04-22 12:00:00-04:00 -- America/New_York
2025-04-22 17:00:00+01:00 -- Europe/London
2025-04-22 16:00:00+00:00 -- UTC
2025-04-22 21:30:00+05:30 -- Asia/Kolkata
2025-04-23 01:00:00+09:00 -- Asia/Tokyo
  • Also see:
    • What's the difference between Instant and LocalDateTime?
    • A Comprehensive Look at Dates and Timestamps in Apache Spark™ 3.0
    • TIMESTAMP type. This is Databricks, so beware if you're using OSS Spark there might be some differences, I've not checked.
  1. Parquet doesn't have any native "timestamp" type. So you can store it
    • as a string. I recommend ISO format, with timzeone in ±HH:mm format (offset-Z in https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/sql-ref-datetime-pattern.html).
    • as a number (How to write TIMESTAMP logical type (INT96) to parquet, using ParquetWriter?), which would a lot more complicated. E.g. parquet-tools inspect <a parquet file from delta table with a timestamp column> will show you that columns of timestamp are stored as physical_type: INT96 inside the underlying parquet files.
  2. When you insert into a delta table, if you ensure your source is timezone aware, then what you're inserting is the exact "instant". Which is what you want. E.g. an ISO format string with timezone, a datetime object with tzinfo set in pyspark, ...
  3. When you insert a timezone-agnostic timestamp (id = 12, 22 below), Spark attaches the current spark session's timezone to the given timestamp to convert it to an instant before storing. Thus giving you inconsistent results.
  4. When you read this data, Spark will take the instant and convert it to the Spark session's timezone. So e.g. if you print it using date_format(ts_ts, "yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssXXX") you'll see Spark session's timezone, see ts_tz_str column in output below.
delta_table = 'delta.`/dbfs/tmp/tz_test`'
spark.sql(f'create table if not exists {delta_table} (id INT, write_tz STRING, ts_str STRING, ts_ts TIMESTAMP)')
spark.sql(f'truncate table {delta_table}')

tz_str = '2025-05-14 12:00:00Z'
notz_str = '2025-05-14 12:00:00'

spark.conf.set("spark.sql.session.timeZone", "UTC")
spark.sql(f'''insert into {delta_table} values 
          (11, '{spark.conf.get("spark.sql.session.timeZone")}', '{tz_str}', TIMESTAMP '{tz_str}')''')
spark.sql(f'''insert into {delta_table} values 
          (12, '{spark.conf.get("spark.sql.session.timeZone")}', '{notz_str}', TIMESTAMP '{notz_str}')''')

spark.conf.set("spark.sql.session.timeZone", "America/New_York")
spark.sql(f'''insert into {delta_table} values 
          (21, '{spark.conf.get("spark.sql.session.timeZone")}', '{tz_str}', TIMESTAMP '{tz_str}')''')
spark.sql(f'''insert into {delta_table} values 
          (22, '{spark.conf.get("spark.sql.session.timeZone")}', '{notz_str}', TIMESTAMP '{notz_str}')''')

spark.conf.set("spark.sql.session.timeZone", "UTC")
spark.sql(f'''select id,'{spark.conf.get("spark.sql.session.timeZone")}' as read_tz,write_tz,ts_str,date_format(ts_ts, "yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssXXX") as ts_tz_str,ts_ts,unix_timestamp(ts_ts) as epoch from {delta_table}''').s()
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.session.timeZone", "America/New_York")
spark.sql(f'''select id,'{spark.conf.get("spark.sql.session.timeZone")}' as read_tz,write_tz,ts_str,date_format(ts_ts, "yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssXXX") as ts_tz_str,ts_ts,unix_timestamp(ts_ts) as epoch from {delta_table}''').s()
